strengths: Novel dual-objective problem formulation (RAA and RR) with clear practical motivation for safe RL and worst-case optimization

Well-motivated and proven necessity of state augmentation (Figure 2, Theorem 3) with clear intuition for why non-augmented policies fail
Principled algorithmic design (DO-HJ-PPO) that directly leverages theoretical decompositions through special Bellman updates and generalized advantage estimation

strengths: Rigorous theoretical contributions with elegant decomposition results (Theorems 1-3) showing RAA and RR problems reduce to compositions of simpler HJ-RL problems

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 environments with diverse baselines (Lagrangian, HJ-RL, STL/LTL, MORL) showing DOHJ-PPO consistently ranks first or second
Strong and consistent empirical results with clear performance metrics (success rate, partial success, achievement time) and ablation studies
Thoughtful appendix addressing theoretical-practical distinctions and explaining why temporal logic decompositions don't apply to HJ value functions

Fundamental limitation from state augmentation requirement: Non-augmented policies cannot solve these problems optimally, requiring memory which limits applicability and increases state dimensionality

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation with clear applications (safe arrival, multi-target achievement)
Rigorous mathematical framework with formal decomposition theorems (Theorems 1-3) for RAA and RR problems
Careful treatment of state augmentation necessity with theoretical justification (Theorem 3)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple continuous control environments
Strong empirical performance relative to baselines, especially as tasks become more difficult

Algorithm design contains ad-hoc elements lacking theoretical justification: coupled resets improve performance empirically but without principled motivation; multiple network learning strategy not theoretically grounded

Lack of convergence analysis: no theoretical guarantees for DOHJ-PPO convergence, sample complexity, or formal justification for why stochastic approximations work in practice

strengths: Novel and well-motivated problem formulations (RAA and RR) addressing practical safe RL scenarios with clear motivation from mission-critical applications
Strong theoretical contributions with Theorems 1-2 providing non-trivial and elegant decomposition results that enable composition of HJ-RL problems
Theorem 3 properly addresses the state augmentation sufficiency with rigorous proof, showing why the specific augmentation structure is necessary and sufficient
Comprehensive experiments across four diverse continuous control environments (Hopper, F16, SafetyGym, HalfCheetah) with consistent performance gains over multiple baseline categories
Careful algorithmic design (DOHJ-PPO) that principally leverages theoretical decompositions via coupled resets, with empirical justification for design choices
Valuable technical insight in Appendix L distinguishing these decompositions from temporal logic predicate algebra, clarifying subtle but important theoretical differences
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figures 1-2) and meaningful evaluation metrics (success, partial success, convergence speed)
Robustness validation with stochastic dynamics (Section 8.3) showing strong performance even with injected noise
weaknesses: Fundamental scope limitation: only handles 2-objective compositions; extending to arbitrary compositions explicitly acknowledged as future work, significantly limiting generalizability

Critical theory-practice gap: Theorems 1-2 assume deterministic dynamics; extension to stochastic case via SRABE involves non-commuting expectation-extrema operators with only empirical validation and no formal guarantees

Algorithm requires multiple actor-critic pairs increasing computational complexity, though no wall-clock time comparisons provided; claim of 'little to no tuning' contradicted by substantial hyperparameter variation across environments (Tables 2-5)
Coupled reset strategy is empirically validated but lacks theoretical justification; unclear why this is superior to alternatives like independent training followed by fine-tuning

Baseline fairness concerns: CPPO variants appear somewhat strawman-like with fairest formulation (v1) performing worst while 'naive and seemingly unfair' variant (v3) performing best; stronger baselines from recent constrained RL literature would strengthen claims
Experimental domains remain relatively structured with simple environments; evaluation on more complex real-world systems or high-dimensional observations would strengthen contributions
Binary success metric doesn't capture partial progress; no comparison with simple alternatives like weighted reward sums with standard PPO

Missing critical ablations: coupled resets necessity, independent vs. concurrent training of objectives, sensitivity to discount factor γ; limited discussion of failure modes and incompatible objectives
